text: Not every line on a bank statement has a pre-existing counterpart in Payables, Receivables, or Payroll. Bank fees, interest earned, miscellaneous charges all show up with nothing in Oracle waiting to match them. This lesson covers the object that fills that gap: the external transaction.

An external cash transaction represents cash activity that was never recorded within the application — a monthly maintenance fee, interest earned, a wire transfer fee, a bank adjustment. None of these start as a Payables invoice or a Receivables transaction. The bank statement is the first place they appear in writing.

Most often these get created directly from a statement line during reconciliation, exactly the scenario from lesson eleven — a Cash Manager hits a line with no counterpart and creates the transaction on the spot. They can also be created manually ahead of time if a recurring charge is already known. Every external transaction needs an amount, a date, a bank account, and an account for the Create Accounting process to post to.

Like every other Cash Management transaction, an external transaction must be reconciled before it can be accounted. One created directly from a statement line is, by definition, immediately reconciled to that same line. Worth knowing ahead of the next lesson: a bank transfer isn't a separate kind of object — it actually creates two external transactions, an outflow and an inflow, and everything here about reconciliation and accounting applies to both.

A fictional example: First Continental Bank deducts a $35 monthly fee from Harborview Metals Inc's operating account, and the Cash Manager creates a matching external transaction right there during reconciliation. Up next, lesson sixteen: bank account transfers, built from exactly this object.
